From the pipeline, there are these warnings about encoding types.  It looks like this predominantly big endian (and ENC_NA has the same value), but there is one usage of ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN..

The other warnings from check_typed_item_calls.py are bogus (assuming that there is an unused bit inside the status).

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-bluetooth.c:6594 proto_tree_add_item called for FT_UINT16 field "hf_btad_apple_homekit_category"  - with bad encoding - "ENC_NA" - {'ENC_BIG_ENDIAN', 'ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN', 'ENC_HOST_ENDIAN'} allowed

Does it make sense to have these as a structure and append/modify as the options are found rather than individual entries?

Ah, good catch. The first entry is a leftover.

I don't have a strong opinion here. Do we have a recommendation on when to start using a structure.

I guess it depends on how related the data is and how would/could it expand?  Would the current 3 items expand into their own separate structures or is the proto data really just capturing "all Bluetooth Apple data in the packet".  If it's the latter, definitely should have a structure to make it obvious that's what's happening.
